meta.name: result-vocabulary
meta.description: Language-neutral expected verifier outcomes for the normalized result vocabulary (spec/results.md): the derived verdict ('valid' | 'invalid' | 'unsupported', with ok == (verdict=='valid') as an invariant), the verdict_reason channel (non-null iff 'unsupported' — it names a limitation of the VERIFIER, never a defect of the capsule), and the qualifier vocabulary (the weaker-claim facts that must reach any renderer beside a valid verdict). expected.qualifiers is an EXACT array in the spec-defined order, compared after stripping x- vendor entries from the result — cross-lane emission cannot drift by omission or invention. Several vectors verify the SAME capsule bytes under different host configurations (allowlist, accept_versions): the host-relative qualifiers are facts about THIS verification, which is exactly why they can never be capsule members. The encrypted vector pins encrypted_outer_only as PER-RESULT: the outer L2 result of an encrypted capsule carries it; the L3 result of the decrypted inner never does.
meta.no_warranty: Conformance fixtures only; not production templates or advice.

notes: 'allowlist' names keypairs in keys_file ([] = verify with no allowlist). 'accept_versions' is passed to the verifier's declared-accepted-versions policy option (spec/versioning.md 'Host policy').

'allowlist_literal' entries reach the verifier VERBATIM — they are never resolved against keys_file, because a MALFORMED entry is by construction one no keypair can produce. When present, the effective allowlist is the resolved 'allowlist' names (empty if the vector declares none) plus the literal entries; the collection-level default never applies. This is the only way to express allowlist hygiene at the registry surface.

The encrypted fixture is a byte-copy of ../tamper-detection/output/clean-encrypted.capsule (fresh encryption is not deterministic); its signer and recipient keypairs are mirrored into this collection's keys_file as encrypted_originator / recipient.

vectors.name: unqualified-valid
vectors.note: The strongest honest shape: committed signer set, bound actors, walked chain, matching allowlist. The ONLY capsule allowed an empty qualifiers array — every weaker shape below must say so on the verdict.

vectors.name: maximally-qualified-valid

expected.notes_includes: the signer set is not bound by the seal

vectors.note: The trust.md threat-table capsule: no signer_commitment, no participants, zero events, verified with no allowlist. It VERIFIES — each is a weaker claim made honestly — and every reduced assurance is a qualifier a conforming renderer must surface beside the verdict. A host that says just 'verified' about this capsule is the failure mode this collection exists to kill.

vectors.name: encrypted-outer-l2
vectors.note: Clean encrypted capsule verified at L2 without a recipient key: the seal is verified, the content unread, the chain deferred — a scope fact the verdict must carry. Lanes with L3 decrypt the same bytes with 'recipient' and MUST NOT find encrypted_outer_only on the inner result: the qualifier is per-result, not per-capsule.

vectors.name: allowlist-no-match
vectors.note: The SAME bytes as unqualified-valid under a non-matching allowlist: valid math, zero trusted signers — a PASS that must never be silent about why trusted=false everywhere. First registry pin of the allowlist-matched-no-signer advisory (the lanes that never emitted it gain it here).

vectors.name: malformed-allowlist-entry
vectors.note: The SAME bytes again, under a host allowlist whose only entry is unusable ('zz' is not 64 hex chars). spec/results.md defines trust_not_evaluated on the EFFECTIVE (well-formed) allowlist, so every lane must drop the malformed entry, note that it did, and report that trust was never evaluated — NOT no_trusted_signer, which would claim a real allowlist was applied and matched nothing. The distinction is the difference between 'this host never asked' and 'this host asked and the answer was no'. Pinned cross-lane rather than per-lane on purpose: this exact divergence shipped once (three lanes filtered, two tested the raw set) while every lane's own trust tests passed, so only an expectation all five compare against can keep it closed.

vectors.name: policy-version-not-accepted

expected.notes_includes: not in the declared accepted set

vectors.note: The same bytes with a host policy excluding 0.7. Integrity is intact (ok stays true — the SDK reports, the host decides), and the policy verdict is a qualifier: the v1.0 gate names policy failure as a distinction hosts must be able to make without out-of-band wording. First vector able to exercise accepted_by_policy at all.

vectors.name: unsupported-newer-verdict
vectors.note: Internally coherent under the 9.9 domain strings; only the version gate refuses it. verdict 'unsupported' with a machine-readable reason keeps 'this verifier is too old' distinguishable from tamper at the NORMALIZED surface — no substring matching on lane-specific errors.

vectors.name: unsupported-older-verdict
vectors.note: The other refusal direction: an era older than any this line of implementations has supported. Not evidence of tampering; verdict_reason says which direction, so a host can route to an implementation retaining the 0.1 rules.

vectors.name: invalid-tamper-verdict
vectors.note: unqualified-valid with program.md rewritten post-seal. verdict 'invalid', verdict_reason null (an invalid capsule's causes live in errors/failing, which have their own vocabulary), qualifiers empty — qualifiers only ever qualify a VALID verdict.
